answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock $100 in a vault before it can bid on jobs, whether composing a sonnet or diagnosing a diseased vine. Deposits stay locked for 30 days and cannot back two identities at once. Creating 1,000 bidding identities therefore ties up $100,000 for a month. This does not eliminate fake identities, but makes each additional identity consume capital the attacker cannot spend elsewhere.
